text:
Muscle lactate production increases when glycolysis is activated at the onset of exercise, because pyruvate is formed faster than mitochondria can oxidize it and lactate dehydrogenase converts the surplus to lactate. Pyruvate must still be formed from glucose breakdown; without it, lactate production falls. The increase is typical of intense exercise and heavy fast-twitch recruitment, including when oxygen supply is limited.

CONFIDENCE: 92
